precepts.text: The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is. Christian commentaries put Isaiah 33 entirely in Hezekiah's past so the apologists can say it already happened; the scripture has a double meaning.
precepts.point: Rabshakeh had cried in the Jews' language: let not Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord; make an agreement with me by a present and I will carry you to a land like your own; which of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of my hand? The people held their peace at the king's commandment.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
When you go to the Christian commentaries on Isaiah 33, many of them refer it back to this history: Hezekiah, the king of Assyria, and the angel that wiped them all out. They try to keep every prophecy in the past, as history that already happened. That is why the apologists love to say, that happened already: they read a Christian commentary that said so.

But the scriptures have dual meanings. Job says he “would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” We all want to know the secrets of wisdom, and they are double to that which is written. You read something, but it has a double meaning behind it. That's how the scriptures are written.

So Isaiah 33:1, “Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee!”, was Assyria; but guess who also does that today? The United States of America. To spoil means to rob: the oil of Venezuela, the riches of Libya and of Saddam Hussein, Iran, which did nothing to America. “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”. The history of 2 Kings 19 happened, and the same word speaks to our day.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Moses was held on the mount a long season and told many wondrous things, the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded, “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” How did Moses hide them? Hosea says the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison, like a metaphor: you speak of a tree, but you are not really talking about a tree. When Genesis speaks of the trees in the garden, it is comparing trees to human beings. It is all going into Adam's kingdom, but it is hidden.

Job calls those hidden things the secrets of wisdom: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are the things Moses hid.

And they are double. You read a scripture, but it is not saying only one thing; it is saying two things. Many times we read a scripture and think we have it, then read it again and the Most High takes us to see something else on another level. That doesn't make what we first saw wrong; there is simply another level to it.

The Lord told Moses to hide these things because they are not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand them, because the Lord “revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

note.label: Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated

precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The scriptures are twofold.

The ten commandments are reiterated here and Israel reminded, because the graven images they knew came from Egypt. But the commandment still pertains today, to spiritual Egypt: against the false images of Christ, the virgin mary statues, the cobblestone at Mecca, buddha and the gods of the east. “Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath” spoke to Egypt then and speaks to spiritual Egypt now.

He is a jealous God, “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.” The secrets of wisdom are double, and both sides of the word stand.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.” The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is: the scriptures often carry a double meaning, speaking of that time and of what is to come.

David’s song is twofold, and David is prophesying. “It is God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me, And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies”: it speaks of David in that moment and of us who are yet to come.

And God exacteth of us less than our iniquity deserves. The Most High requires of us far less: to repent, keep the commandments, and keep the faith in his son Jesus the Christ. For this David gives thanks “among the heathen” and sings praises unto his name, for “He is the tower of salvation for his king: and sheweth mercy to his anointed, unto David, and to his seed for evermore.”

note.label: Jeremiah 50: The Fall of Babylon and the Return of Israel

precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are double. The scriptures are twofold.

So the word the Lord spoke against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet is not spent on one kingdom. It speaks against ancient Babylon and against modern-day Babylon, which is America. “Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach is broken in pieces; her idols are confounded, her images are broken in pieces”: that is to be declared among the nations both times.
